desc:
Count the strictly increasing subsequences of nums that have exactly k elements. Two subsequences are different when they use different sets of indices, even if they contain the same values.

The count can be huge, so return it modulo 1,000,000,007. For nums = [1, 3, 2, 4] and k = 3 the answer is 2 (1, 3, 4 and 1, 2, 4).
hints: Count by length. Let ways[l][i] be the number of strictly increasing subsequences of length l that end exactly at index i. What is ways[1][i]?
ways[l][i] is the sum of ways[l-1][j] over all j < i with nums[j] < nums[i]. The answer is the sum of ways[k][i] over all i. Done naively that is O(k n<sup>2</sup>).

For each level l, sweep i from left to right and keep a Fenwick tree indexed by value rank that holds ways[l-1][j] for the indices already seen. The inner sum is then a prefix query: O(k n log n) in total.
editorial: Layer the DP by subsequence length. A subsequence of length 1 is any single element, so ways[1][i] = 1. A subsequence of length l ending at i is a subsequence of length l-1 ending at some earlier index j with a smaller value, followed by i. Hence ways[l][i] = sum ways[l-1][j] over j < i and nums[j] < nums[i], and the answer is the sum of ways[k][i] over all i (modulo 1,000,000,007).

Evaluating that sum with a loop is O(n) per cell, so O(k n2) overall. Instead process each level in one left-to-right sweep. Compress the values to ranks, and keep a Fenwick (binary indexed) tree where position rank[j] holds ways[l-1][j] for every j already visited. For index i, query the prefix of ranks strictly below rank[i] to get ways[l][i], then insert ways[l-1][i] at rank[i]. Equal values never combine because the query excludes the own rank.
Total time is O(k n log n) and memory O(n) (only the previous level is kept). If at some level every count is zero, the answer is 0 and the loop can stop early.
solution:
from bisect import bisect_left

def countIncreasingOfLengthK(nums, k):
    M = 1000000007
    n = len(nums)
    if k > n:
        return 0
    vals = sorted(set(nums))
    m = len(vals)
    rank = [bisect_left(vals, x) + 1 for x in nums]
    prev = [1] * n
    for _ in range(k - 1):
        tree = [0] * (m + 1)
        cur = [0] * n
        for i in range(n):
            s = 0
            j = rank[i] - 1
            while j > 0:
                s += tree[j]
                j -= j & -j
            cur[i] = s % M
            v = prev[i]
            if v:
                j = rank[i]
                while j <= m:
                    tree[j] += v
                    j += j & -j
        prev = cur
        if not any(prev):
            return 0
    return sum(prev) % M
